# #3075 (lane L-PGP) — the postgres federation-RECEIVE APPLY context
# (`federation_apply_ctx`), used by the migrated `/sync/push` subcollections
# (namespace_meta / namespace_meta_clears, and the further families as they
# land). PARITY, not convenience: the sqlite twin applies these lanes through
# raw `db::*` free functions that consult NO caller identity at all — the
# federation authorization is the PEER-SCOPE gate (`receive_auth::inbound_*_
# authorized`) plus the per-lane crypto attestation, never the local
# owner/tenant gate. Several pg trait methods DO carry a local caller-owns gate
# for their TENANT surfaces (`clear_namespace_standard` #1777/#2545,
# `archive_by_ids` #3193, `archive_restore` #3271); routing a federated apply
# through a tenant-scoped ctx would make the pg receiver refuse rows the sqlite
# receiver applies — a silent cross-backend divergence of exactly the #2488
# shape, whose symptom is two peers answering `get_standard` with different
# governance. Every call site runs AFTER the lane's `receive_auth` verdict, on a
# peer/operator surface (#238 envelope + #29 sig + #30 nonce + #43 enrollment
# all precede it), never a tenant-facing handler; the principal is the attested
# sender so the write stays attributable. Adds NO reach a peer did not have.

# owner-blind sqlite receive loop; every call site runs after the lane's receive_auth
# verdict on a peer/operator surface.

# #955 SECURITY-medium (Track A QC sweep, 2026-05-20), surfaced 2026-09-12 by
# #3623's precheck rewrite — NOT a new bypass. `resolve_namespace_standard` on
# postgres performs a SUBSTRATE-INTERNAL policy read: it is called by other
# trait methods that have already resolved their own caller context, and the
# standard memory it reads is governance policy the substrate must see
# regardless of `metadata.scope`. `for_agent("governance")` would mismatch the
# standard's owner and silently drop the policy row when scope=private,
# breaking governance resolution for private namespaces. The older precheck
# did not detect this call site; #3623 restored that coverage, which is what
# this entry records.
